newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish Cypriots to stop march on ghost town.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Cypriots to stop march on ghost town.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot authorities say they will stop a planned march by ultra-nationalist Turks entering the empty Greek Cypriot town of Varosha, Turkish Cypriot deputy leader Serdar Denktash told Reuters on Wednesday.

"We don't agree with these kind of protests. The government has come to agreement that we will find ways to stop it. Even if they try to make a demonstration close to Maras (Varosha) we will stop it," Serdar Denktash said.

Turkish Cypriot ultra-nationalist leader Mehmet Arslan at the weekend called on followers to enter Varosha, known as Maras in Turkish, and lay claim to houses there in a demonstration to be held on March 2.
But Arslan was quoted in Turkish Cypriot newspapers on Wednesday as saying that he no longer planned to go ahead with the demonstration.
The planned demonstration was denounced by Greek and Greek Cypriot leaders as a provocation and Turkish officials said they did not back the march.

Turkish Cypriot leader and father of Serdar Denktash, Rauf Denktash, earlier threatened to open Varosha to Turkish Cypriot settlement if the Cypriot government in the south went ahead with a planned missile purchase from Russia.

Varosha, a seaside resort until the Turkish invasion in 1974, lies between the Turkish Cypriot north of the island and the Greek Cypriot south. The United Nations holds Turkey responsible for the maintenance of the status quo there.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia backed by the military ruling in Athens at the time.

The international community, with the exception of Turkey, recognises the Greek Cypriot administration in the south as the only government on the island. The Turkish Cypriot breakaway administration in the north is only recognised by Turkey.
